prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1204; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, no police report filed at scene. Insured reports the other vehicle stopped suddenly and was struck from behind. Recorded statement scheduled for next business day.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Reports neck and lower back discomfort following impact, has not yet seen a physician. States the vehicle was driven away from scene and is currently at a repair shop for estimate. Claimant is not represented by counsel and confirmed this on the recording.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from the insured. Rear bumper damage visible on the claimant's vehicle, minor crush to the trunk panel on the insured's vehicle. Scene diagram reviewed, consistent with the reported sequence. Liability appears clear pending confirmation of the insured's following distance.

Entry 4: Claimant contacted to follow up. Reports ongoing lower back strain, pain worse when sitting for long periods. Has scheduled an appointment with a primary care provider and will forward records once available. Explained the medical authorization form and the process for submitting bills. Claimant asked questions about rental vehicle coverage, which was discussed.

Entry 5: Received repair estimate for the claimant's vehicle from the shop. Medical documentation not yet received. Diary set for follow-up on records and reassessment of injury status. File remains open with liability accepted on the insured's side, bodily injury evaluation ongoing.
